channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Protected: Three AI Tactics To Triple Your Caseload
item.description: Firms that have embedded AI into every workflow are tripling attorney capacity, increasing settlement value, and resolving cases 60+ days faster. Those that haven't are falling behind. Here are three tactics top plaintiff firms use to embed AI firm-wide while raising the bar on work product.

item.title: Trial Court celebrates Women’s History Month
item.description: Some 500 women from across the state and beyond turned out for the Annual Massachusetts Trial Court Women’s History Month ceremony and conference held recently in Norwood.

item.title: Museum provides backdrop for ALA Boston chapter meeting
item.description: The Boston chapter of the Association of Legal Administrators recently held its annual meeting at the Museum of African American History in Boston.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump administration from detaining thousands of refugees
item.description: A federal judge in Boston blocked the Trump administration's policy to detain refugees without green cards after one year, ruling it unlawful.

item.title: Campbell’s motion to strike audit case kicked up to full SJC
item.description: Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court will review whether Auditor Diana DiZoglio can be represented by outside counsel in her audit dispute against the Attorney General.

item.title: Delaware dog custody battle wraps up with unexpected auction
item.description: Delaware's Chancery Court ended a lengthy custody battle over a goldendoodle named Tucker by ordering a sealed bid auction between the estranged owners.

item.title: Footnote in legal-mal case spawns debate over tolling
item.description: Massachusetts judge dismisses legal malpractice suit as untimely, ruling adverse court decisions put clients on notice of harm despite ongoing litigation.

item.title: Securities – Standing
item.description: Where claims of conversion, breach of fiduciary duty, negligence and violation of the Uniform Securities Act (G.L.c. 110A) were dismissed for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, the judgment of dismissal must be vacated because the plaintiffs' allegations of injury suffice to establish standing.

item.title: Products liability – Preemption – Medical device
item.description: Where a plaintiff has brought a product liability action asserting personal injury claims against the designers, manufacturers and sellers of a medical device that failed during her hysterectomy surgery, a motion to dismiss should be denied because the plaintiff’s claims are not preempted despite the defendants’ contention that only the FDA can enforce violations of the Food and Drug Cosmetic Act.

item.title: Employment – Referral bonus – Wage Act
item.description: Where two plaintiffs have brought a putative class action alleging that their former employer withheld payments that they had earned through its employee referral program, their claim under the Massachusetts Wage Act must be dismissed because the referral bonus payments at issue are not “wages” under the statute, but they have plausibly alleged a claim for breach of contract.
